content.intro: This lesson covers preparing fine-tuning datasets through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Customize an existing model only after establishing a baseline and deciding prompting or retrieval is insufficient. Dataset permissions, compute, evaluation, and versioned artifacts all matter.
content.why_it_matters: For task-specific training examples, distinguish the training objective from the evaluation goal. items.title: Data cleaning and deduplication
items.text: Data cleaning and deduplication addresses how information is prepared, described, versioned, or governed. Validate the input, keep source and access metadata, handle duplicates and missing values deliberately, and test the downstream effect of a data change rather than treating the data pipeline as invisible plumbing.

items.title: Data rights and sensitive information
items.text: Data rights and sensitive information is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice task-specific training examples within preparing fine-tuning datasets: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
